name: Schizachyrium

project_scope.note: The current project pool has one canonical Schizachyrium anchor; species taxonomy/range decisions remain in the species package.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Native little bluestem shows DISTINCT relatively tight bunches and many SHORT silvery racemes terminating separate leafy upper branches. Introduced KR bluestem instead presents several LONG fingerlike racemes gathered into one terminal panicle; both require same-plant leaf collars and paired spikelet macro.
priority: numerous separate SHORT terminal or axillary racemes throughout upper culm
true leaf collar and mature paired spikelets
short terminal fuzzy racemes on branchlets

comparisons.rule: Schizachyrium scatters many short racemes across branched upper stems; Bothriochloa concentrates its rames into a more unified terminal head whose node hair and branch architecture are major ID clues.
Anatherum glomeratum builds a dense brushlike fluffy crown; Schizachyrium scoparium shows repeated short racemes terminating separate upper branchlets.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.title: KR BLUESTEM vs LITTLE BLUESTEM — our Central Texas native/invasive decision
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.memory_rule: A FEW LONG fingers together (KR) versus MANY SHORT fuzzy racemes on SEPARATE upper branches (little bluestem).
quick_split: KR / Bothriochloa ischaemum — introduced Old World bluestem; terminal panicle typically 3–8 or more elongated fingerlike spikelet-bearing branches. Leaf UPPER surface just above collar may have stiff papilla-based hairs. Node hair sources conflict; not a single-character proof.

Little bluestem / Schizachyrium scoparium — Hays native, generally dense persistent bunch; many short racemes arise from different branches in the upper plant and become silvery/fluffy in fruit. Roots/leaf collar and actual spikelet pairs strengthen ID.
field_crew_sequence: Photograph rooted whole clump and top-to-bottom reproductive architecture.
Trace WHERE each raceme originates: all near one terminal center = KR candidate; dispersed short units on many upper culm branches = little bluestem candidate.
At 10×, inspect KR upper leaf surface right above collar for papilla-based hairs; check true ligule on same culm.
Check paired sessile fertile/pedicelled companion spikelet details with 1-mm scale; where unresolved label bluestem sp.
Before removal or seed collection, rule out native cane bluestem and silver bluestem plus introduced Kleberg bluestem.
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.node_hair_caution: Do not enforce smooth KR nodes: Texas A&M calls songarica nodes hairless; local UT Austin morphological work reports short or appressed hairs. Use combined characters. Cane bluestem tends to bear a pronounced BEARD at nodes.

items.label: KR bluestem — straw-colored flowering racemes
items.image_role: Actual archived source-labelled mature flowering spike, hand scale, two long racemes visible
items.caption: Two long, nearly parallel flowering racemes bearing numerous small awned units. These actual pixels do not contain stem nodes, leaf collar, upper blade hairs, rootstock or the entire plant's 3–8 terminal branches.
items.why_it_matters: Shows characteristic elongated fingerlike reproductive branches instead of little bluestem's many SHORT flowering segments distributed over the upper plant.
items.creator: Sam Kieschnick
items.photo_status: Original local JPEG personally pixel-inspected for visible raceme and awn-bearing units, source determination remains provisional, license version shorthand as originally archived.

items.label: KR bluestem — 3 radiating long racemes
items.image_role: Actual archived source-labelled photo, several long flowering branches spreading from clustered lower portion
items.caption: Several dry narrow flowering branches visible against fingers; branching geometry is clear. Their tiny spikelet glumes and the true node collar or hairless vs hairy stem-node distinction are not resolved.
items.why_it_matters: Shows how separate long racemes converge toward one clustered reproductive head, unlike scattered short axillary racemes of little bluestem.
items.creator: Sam Kieschnick
items.photo_status: Existing local JPEG physically inspected and only gross head architecture annotated; exact CC BY version unresolved.

items.label: Little bluestem — dense perennial bunch
items.image_role: Actual archived overall green perennial bunch / upright vegetative shoots
items.caption: A dense clump of fine upright culms and narrow leaves; its base and upper culms are visible. This is NOT an adequate view of an individual flowering raceme, glume/awn, ligule, or a botanically proven species from anatomy.
items.why_it_matters: Learn the usually dense narrow bunch form of native little bluestem, contrasting with KR's often broader sprawling crowns in heavily managed/disturbed vegetation.
items.creator: TheMongrelKoi
items.photo_status: Original real JPEG pixels inspected; image licensed CC0 in original canonical card, original taxon label source-based.

items.label: Little bluestem — branched upper flowering architecture
items.image_role: Actual central Texas source-labelled photo showing straw/reddish stems and upper branched grass, with hand for scale
items.caption: Several slender straw-colored branching culms stand in a prairie. The photo allows a gross habit cue, but the precise origin of any single short raceme and silky paired-spikelet hairs cannot be individually certified from these pixels.
items.why_it_matters: Field-stage upright branched culms are a useful context for finding the separate short racemes of native little bluestem.
items.creator: Jean H.
items.photo_status: Original local central-Texas JPEG inspected for gross culm anatomy, NC/SA license preserved; NO arrows placed on alleged microscopic seed hairs.
